approach: Replace existing boolean flags controlling detection/evaluation phases—`inside`, `parse_mode`, and `is_nest`—with integer-based nest tracking (`nest_level`), incremented upon entering a snippet block via either opening delimiter (`-{1,}8<-{1,}` alone) or closing counterpart (same pattern indicating termination), decremented symmetrically on exit. Maintain equivalent truth-value semantics (`inside = bool(nest_level)`) elsewhere while introducing nuanced conditional guards: allow evaluation (`parse_mode=True`) only when neither actively escaping nor currently within a raw fence block (`not in_raw_block`) irrespective of nest depth; conversely restrict actual parsing actions (extracting/include content) solely to topmost frame (`nest_level==1`) to avoid double-processing intermediary wrappers. Adjust preprocessor initialization accordingly and update per-line handling branching logic around matched delimiters to reflect nest-depth awareness rather than relying on stale booleans vulnerable to incorrect state propagation across recursive layers — particularly critical given how section markers masquerade as ordinary lines needing passthrough when embedded but triggering extraction when exposed at surface level.
hypothesis: To support nested snippets, I need to ensure recursive processing continues beyond the depth where outer snippets contain inner markers. Currently, two modes prevent recursion: when inside a raw block (`in_raw_block=True`) because these contexts shouldn't evaluate their contents recursively, and during initial parsing due to continued mode after discovering deep nesting. Since enabling recursion breaks core escaping/inlining semantics—like preventing proper handling of comment-out statements (;---8<--) and semicolon-prefixed ignored directives—I must safeguard the system by limiting recursion strictly to non-raw-block scenarios while keeping top-level mode mechanics untouched. This means preserving current special-markers logic unmodified yet permitting recursive dives when none apply. Implementing targeted adjustments thus resolves both nested snippet inclusion needs and preserves existing correct behaviors.
